title.narrative: Increased resilience of young women and men in Tripoli and surroundings

description.narrative: 65 Young women and men between the age of 16 and 25 from Tripoli and its surrounding received the following resilience activities: PSS, Positive and non-Violent Communications training, Technical Vocational Training Education, Digital Skills training, Humanitarian Principles Training, and Apprenticeship enrolment in private sector.

IRT phase 4 aim to support Young women and men between 15 and 26 at risks of violent extremism to choose and recognize the existence of positive nonviolent pathways in Tripoli city, in 8 “hotspot “areas where significant recruitment to violent extremism has occurred and where violence ideology, grievances and radicalization are increasing.

The project fits under the prevention pillar within the contest strategy as the following:
Prevent: The purpose of Prevent is to stop people from becoming drawn into or supporting terrorism. This includes countering terrorist ideology and challenging those who promote it; supporting individuals who are especially vulnerable to becoming radicalised; and working with sectors and institutions where the risk of radicalisation is assessed to be high.
The Increased Resilience of young women and men project is implemented in Tripoli city, in hotspot “areas where significant recruitment to violent extremism has occurred and where violence ideology, grievances and radicalization are increasing. The project is targeting especially youth that are vulnerable to becoming radicalised or already involved in violent acts, in order to support them to choose and recognize the existence of positive nonviolent pathways.
Also, the project is directly working with local institutions whether governmental, Civil society organizations, or private sector where the risk of radicalization is high, in order to support them and build their institutional and technical capacities to reduce violent extremism risks and to identify, engage, support and mentor youth that are at high risk of becoming radicalized.
The project will contribute to the multiple outcomes around 1) increased resilience of individuals and communities in areas where young people are at risk of recruitment to violent extremism, 2) strengthening institutional and technical capacity 3) strengthen relationship with community stakeholders 4) enhance vocational skills.
